extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders invited to comment on Railroad Retirement Board information collections; respondents who complete RRB forms; OIRA/OMB reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice from the Railroad Retirement Board describing multiple Information Collection Requests (ICRs) submitted to OMB, including form titles, purposes, burden estimates, proposed changes, affected public, and instructions for submitting public comments under the Paperwork Reduction Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment topics under the Paperwork Reduction Act
rubrics_metrics.description: RRB invites comments on the proposed collections of information to determine (1) the practical utility of the collections; (2) the accuracy of the estimated burden of the collections; (3) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information that is the subject of collection; and (4) ways to minimize the burden of collections on respondents, including the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proper consideration, submit comments addressing one or more of these four topics. Comments should be specific to the ICR at issue and may propose improvements or alternative collection methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments must contain OMB control number and be timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments to the RRB or OIRA must contain the OMB control number of the ICR. For proper consideration of your comments, it is best if the RRB and OIRA receive them within 30 days of the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the exact OMB control number when commenting. Submit via the provided addresses/emails or reginfo.gov as instructed; late comments may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICR metadata elements to be published
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Information Collection Request includes: Title; OMB Control Number; Form(s) submitted; Type of request (e.g., revision, extension without change); Affected public; Abstract; Changes proposed; The burden estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements should be clearly stated in the notice so reviewers/commenters can evaluate purpose, scope, and impact. The official PDF and XML are available for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimate reporting format
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden estimates are reported by form with fields: Form No.; Annual responses; Time (minutes); Burden (hours); and totals across forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices should present per-form breakdowns and totals so commenters can assess the estimated respondent workload. Example rows are provided (e.g., G-134: With Assistance 11 responses, 147 minutes, 27 burden hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form completion requirement and consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether completion of a form is required or voluntary is specified; if completion is required to obtain benefits, failure to complete may result in inability to obtain benefits or denial of requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must state if completion is mandatory to obtain benefits or voluntary, and should explain consequences of non-compliance (e.g., inability to pay benefits, denial of waiver request).

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA review purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and approval by OIRA ensures that we impose appropriate paperwork burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA review is the mechanism for checking whether the information collection burden imposed on the public is appropriate; commenters may address whether OIRA approval should or should not be granted based on burden or utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to submit comments (procedural submission requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments and recommendations for the proposed information collection should be sent within 30 days of publication to www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAMain; copies of forms and supporting documents may be obtained from the listed contact (Kennisha Money) or by contacting Brian Foster at the provided address/email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the particular ICR on reginfo.gov by selecting 'Currently under 30-day Review—Open for Public Comments' or by using the search function. Use the listed contact names, addresses, and emails for direct inquiries or to request copies of forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affected public designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ICR specifies the affected public category (for these collections: 'Individuals or Households').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected public designation informs reviewers about who bears the burden; commenters may assess whether the affected public categorization is correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICR change description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices must state whether changes are proposed to the collection and describe those changes (e.g., 'minor editorial change to Form G-134 to change the date under Section 1 "General Instructions"', or 'add a drop-down box `Second Request' at the top of Form G-106').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear description of proposed changes (including explicit wording or UI changes) enables commenters to evaluate whether the change affects burden, clarity, or utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-specific purpose and use — Statement Regarding Contributions and Support (Form G-134; OMB 3220-0099)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form G-134 is used to secure information needed to adequately determine if the applicant meets the one-half support requirement which can affect entitlement to survivor annuity, amount of spouse and survivor annuities, Tier II restored amount, and public service pension offset. One response is completed by each respondent. Completion is required to obtain benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice includes statutory basis (section 2 of the Railroad Retirement Act) and clarifies that the form is necessary to determine eligibility; commenters may address the utility and burden of this specific form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-specific purpose and use — Financial Disclosure Statement (Form DR-423; OMB 3220-0127)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form DR-423 is used to obtain information about an overpaid beneficiary's income, debts, and expenses when the beneficiary indicates they cannot make restitution; the information is used to determine if an overpayment should be waived or to set installment payments. One response is requested of each respondent. Completion is voluntary but failure to provide information may result in denial of the waiver request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice provides statutory authority and related regulations; commenters may evaluate burden estimates and the clarity/utility of the form fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-specific purpose and use — Representative Payee Monitoring (Forms G-99a, G-99c, G-106; OMB 3220-0151)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form G-99a is used to determine whether benefit payments certified to a representative payee have been used for the annuitant's maintenance and personal needs; Form G-99c obtains more detailed information (including specific questions concerning representative payee performance) and is used to determine whether the payee should continue; Form G-106 solicits information from a custodian about the payee's performance and annuitant well-being. Completion is required to retain benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice explains statutory authority (Section 12 of RRA) and monitoring purpose; proposed changes to forms (e.g., adding a 'Second Request' dropdown on G-106) are listed for comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-specific purpose and use — Earnings Information Request (Form G-19-F; OMB 3220-0184)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form G-19-F is used to obtain earnings information not previously or erroneously reported by a beneficiary; an annuity is not payable, or is reduced for months in which the beneficiary works for a railroad or earns more than prescribed amounts. One response is requested of each respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice references statutory basis and applicable CFR parts; commenters may address burden and whether the form fields capture necessary information (e.g., date they stopped working).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative payee evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms (notably G-99c) contain specific questions concerning the representative payee's performance and are used by the RRB to determine whether or not the representative payee should continue in that capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation centers on whether funds were used for the annuitant's current maintenance and personal needs and whether the payee remains concerned with the annuitant's welfare; commenters may suggest improvements to the evaluation questions or monitoring frequency.
